questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

questions.passage: Tench were long called doctor fish, on the belief that sick fish rubbed against their slime and were cured, and the belief survived into print for three centuries. questions.stem: According to the text, what problem did photographing the despatches solve?

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how the meaning of the word changed after it entered English. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The English word “decoy” comes from the Dutch eendenkooi, a duck cage.
  • The first ponds of this type in England were built in the 1660s by Dutch builders.
  • The word at first named the pond, not the wooden birds set out on the water.
  • The wooden birds were called “stales” in the seventeenth century.
  • By 1800 “decoy” had come to mean the wooden birds as well.

choices.content: Entering English as the name of the pond itself, the word had by 1800 spread to the wooden birds, which the seventeenth century had called stales.

choices.label: D
choices.content: All three phrases entered general English between 1500 and 1600.

questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The red junglefowl of southern Asia is the ancestor of every domestic chicken, but the date at which the two parted has proved hard to fix. Bones alone are unreliable: a junglefowl and an early domestic bird are nearly identical in the ground, and chicken bones travel downward through soft deposits into layers far older than themselves. Claims of very early domestication have repeatedly collapsed when the bones responsible were dated directly rather than by the layer they were found in.

choices.content: Direct dating of bones has confirmed that chickens were domesticated very early.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Domestic chickens and junglefowl can be told apart easily from their bones.

choices.content: The word has always meant a building in which animals of any kind are kept.

choices.label: D
